THE IDEA

Correct the failures.
Reuse what helps.

Vision-language-action models can perform diverse manipulation tasks, yet reliable real-world execution remains challenging. Evo-RL turns execution feedback into policy improvement through an iterative cycle of data collection and training.

Starting from a demonstration-trained policy, Evo-RL alternates between intervention-based refinement and advantage-guided fine-tuning. Human corrections focus limited supervision on the policy’s current weaknesses. Advantage estimates identify useful segments from demonstrations and autonomous rollouts, helping retain learned skills and prioritize efficient behavior as experience accumulates.

Compared with demonstration-only fine-tuning, the first Evo-RL round increases attempt success by 65.51 percentage points on insertion and 21.11 percentage points on folding. A second insertion round reaches 92.16%. The accumulated experience forms RW-RL, which supports the learning process.

Two challenges during deployment.

TARGETED HUMAN CORRECTIONS

Recover in unfamiliar states

Successful demonstrations may rarely cover the states caused by policy errors. An operator corrects the robot when it struggles, then returns control to the policy. These actions supply supervision where the current policy needs it.

SELECTIVE EXPERIENCE REUSE

Focus the next policy update

As experience grows, repeatedly fine-tuning on the entire accumulated dataset becomes costly. Evo-RL uses advantages to identify useful prior behavior and combine it with new corrections, focusing refinement while helping preserve learned skills.

METHOD

Initialize once. Keep improving.

01 / METHOD

Algorithm 1 starts with demonstration-based initialization. Every subsequent round alternates two policy updates: targeted human-intervention refinement and advantage-guided fine-tuning.

START

Demonstration-based initialization

Fine-tune the pretrained π0.5 VLA policy on teleoperated demonstrations to establish initial task competence.

  1. 1

    Collect corrections. Refine recovery.

    Deploy the current policy, collect human actions in challenging states, and fine-tune on demonstrations mixed with human-controlled segments from successful intervention episodes.

  2. 2

    Estimate advantages. Refine behavior.

    Learn a value model from complete trajectories. Give selected demonstration segments extra sampling weight, and combine them with human corrections and selected autonomous experience when available.

↻ Deploy the refined policy to begin the next round. Continue from its checkpoint.

ADVANTAGE-GUIDED FINE-TUNING

From trajectory feedback to training segments.

A task-specific visual value model predicts normalized remaining returns. The advantage of an action sequence combines its accumulated reward with the change in estimated value, providing a signal for selecting useful segment starts.

50 actionsadvantage lookahead
Positive · top 10%eligible segment starts
20 actionsretained forward window
Policy training, rewards, and sampling details

The policy receives camera images, proprioception, and a task instruction and generates action chunks using a flow-matching action expert. Human-controlled segments provide correction supervision; complete trajectories support value learning.

The task-specific, vision-only value model predicts a distribution over 201 bins in [−1, 0] using two-hot return targets. Each nonterminal frame receives a time cost of −1. The policy transition immediately before a human takeover receives an additional penalty; terminal reward is zero.

The reported demonstration-selection setting estimates advantages over 50 actions, chooses positive nonterminal starts in the global top 10%, and retains 20-action forward windows. Overlapping or adjacent windows merge within their original episode; padded actions are masked. Original demonstrations remain in the training mixture, with selected demonstration segments sampled more often. Human corrections and selected autonomous segments are mixed in as available.

Successful autonomous rollouts enter policy training once autonomous execution surpasses the demonstration baseline. The learning objective remains flow matching across policy updates.

REAL-ROBOT EVIDENCE

Policy gains across tasks and rounds.

02 / RESULTS

The latest manuscript reports precision insertion on PiperX and garment folding on SO-101, including intervention and RL ablations, a second insertion round, and comparisons under matched human-control budgets.

Read the metrics

SR is attempt success: successful attempts divided by all attempts across units and trials. TP reports completed units per hour; a unit is an insertion pair or a folding stage. Each trial has a five-minute limit.

Attempt success and full-task success are distinct metrics. The supplementary PiperX figure below reports full-task success separately. pp denotes an absolute difference in percentage points.

COMPLEMENTARY UPDATES

Corrections and RL work together

SFT + RL reaches 40.48% insertion SR and SFT + Int. reaches 78.72%. Evo-RL reaches 88.24%, exceeding intervention-only refinement by 9.52 pp and 26.3% in throughput.

ANOTHER LEARNING ROUND

More final-unit completions

Evo-RL R2 raises insertion SR to 92.16% and TP to 67.14 units/h. U₅ completions increase from 5 to 8 out of 10; U₄ falls from 10 to 9, so gains are not uniform across units.

FOLDING RECOVERY

Fewer attempts at a difficult stage

At the spreading stage U₂, completions increase from 17 to 19 while attempts fall from 76 to 36. Overall folding SR reaches 76.67%, with TP rising from 75.78 to 90.00 stages/h.

View per-unit results and training protocol

SFT trains on demonstrations for 2.5 epochs. Each intervention condition first trains on demonstrations for 2.5 epochs, collects one hour of corrections, then fine-tunes on the combined data for another 2.5 epochs. These comparisons match human-control budgets; their training schedules differ.

Additional observation: human assistance in packing

The latest manuscript also reports that the human-control time fraction in SO-101 packing falls from 31.65% to 23.26%, while intervention frequency falls by 4.2%. Reduced time under human control therefore coexists with a smaller change in how often assistance is needed.

ON REAL ROBOTS

Watch the policy improve.

03 / DEMOS

Precision insertion tests grasping and alignment on PiperX. Garment folding tests recovery during deformable manipulation on SO-101. Both use dual arms, an external RGB camera, and two wrist cameras.

SUPPORTING THE LEARNING LOOP

RW-RL, the accumulated experience.

04 / DATA

The experience produced by iterative learning forms RW-RL. Demonstrations, human corrections, and autonomous rollouts retain action-source labels and semantic context for differentiated use in training.

1,000+ hours4 embodiments9 scene domains30+ task templates

Explore dataset coverage, annotations, and task examples

RW-RL spans AgiBot G2, Galaxea R1Lite, AgileX PiperX, and SO-101. Synchronized observations, states, and actions link to episode outcomes, controller provenance, intervention boundaries, and hierarchical semantic annotations.
